randomized_labels_control.interpretation: Strong, clean degradation (4.1x drop). The model clearly learns real structure and randomizing tails clearly destroys it.

followup_40_epoch_run.finding: The path-reasoner residual gate (sigmoid(gamma_raw)) remained at essentially its near-zero init value even after 40 epochs on a small synthetic graph -- the path branch had negligible influence on the final score in this run, which explains (not undermines) why the leakage control showed zero measurable effect: there was very little path-branch signal available to leak. The leakage-PREVENTION MECHANISM ITSELF is separately and directly verified in tests/kgr/test_selector.py::test_no_queried_edge_leakage_under_learned_topk (with the gate/selector forced open via zeroed parameters specifically to make leakage detectable) and tests/kgr/test_negative_controls.py -- those tests confirm the exclusion logic is structurally correct. This integration-level null result is flagged as an open question for the Gate 12 confirmatory campaign: does the near-zero-init residual gate open meaningfully within realistic training budgets on real benchmark data, or does it require a longer schedule / higher gate-specific learning rate than the rest of the model? Not resolved in this campaign -- OPEN.
